version.changelog: Keep the first small win, then ask for the starter top-up before the video.

llm.summary: The skill is a real Beatra video-remake workflow, but it also stores broad Beatra credentials, sends installation/environment metadata, and silently self-updates package code by default.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads and persists Beatra state under ~/.beatra, can upload an explicitly named local file, records installed skill paths, detects the agent platform, stores a hostname-derived device name during authorization, and transmits package/platform/installation reference metadata. Some of this supports account and uninstall management, but it is broader than a user would expect from a video-remake skill alone.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses Python helper scripts and device authorization, which are disclosed, but the bundled client checks for updates and replaces package-owned files automatically by default from Beatra discovery/CDN endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow gives strong user-confirmation gates for paid lookups and generation calls, but automatic installation registration and silent auto-updates run during normal client use without a fresh user approval at that moment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists a shared full-scope Beatra device token, installation reference, host metadata, skill inventory, registration cache, and updater state. These are documented and mostly bounded, but the full-scope token and automatic code replacement are high-impact privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core workflow is coherent for social-video lookup, teardown, image generation, speech generation, video generation, task polling, and billing. However, the OAuth scope and bundled client are broader than the stated workflow, including wallet spending, music generation, voices write access, uploads, task cancellation, and generic remote Beatra tool calls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It is not just a prompt-only video workflow: it creates and stores a shared Beatra device token, can spend Beatra credits after workflow confirmations, sends installation/platform metadata to Beatra, and silently updates its own package files unless disabled with python3 scripts/mcp_client.py update --auto off. Install only if you are comfortable with that Beatra account trust model and the broad token scope.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The scanner's least-privilege concern is supported in part: the artifacts disclose network, filesystem, credentials, and shell/Python helper use, but there is no narrow permission manifest and the granted Beatra scope exceeds the specific remake workflow.
[TP4] unexpected: The broad bundled client, OAuth flow, upload helper, registration, uninstall handling, and updater are documented rather than hidden, so this is not malicious tool poisoning, but the trust boundary is materially broader than the headline creative workflow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The silent self-update concern is supported: SKILL.md and the update reference say newer releases are installed automatically by default without separate confirmation, although checksums, fixed URLs, rollback, and package-owned-file limits reduce the risk.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The network self-update mechanism is not necessary to perform a single video teardown/remake task and adds supply-chain and local code-replacement risk.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The installation-registration concern is supported: first use performs a best-effort beatra.installations.register call with package slug, version, platform, and stable external installation reference.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The platform/environment metadata concern is supported: the client detects agent platform from environment signatures or host.json and sends source_platform/source_package_slug on business calls.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The authorization helper persists host metadata and a local skills inventory with install paths. This supports shared credential uninstall decisions, but it is broader than the immediate OAuth token exchange.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The broad OAuth scope concern is supported: authorize.py requests wallet:spend plus image, video, music, speech, voice read/write, artifact, and task scopes, including capabilities not clearly used by this skill.
[SQP-2] expected: Reading captions, author, metrics, comments, and YouTube transcripts is explicitly part of the skill's purpose and is gated by paid lookup confirmations, but users should understand that third-party public social content is sent through Beatra's service.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The automatic-update disclosure exists in SKILL.md and the reference, but the default is still silent installation of replacement package files without contemporaneous approval.
[RA1] unexpected: The self-modification finding is supported as a review concern, not as malicious behavior: the update command and default auto-update path can replace package files, but the artifacts describe fixed sources, checksum verification, rollback, and package-owned-file restrictions.
